headline_drivers: Major multiyear AI compute deal with Microsoft announced September 2025 (Morningstar cites $17B revenue agreement for GPU cloud capacity, underpinning long-term growth and credibility with hyperscalers).

Ongoing AI/HPC infrastructure buildout and Bloom Energy partnership to deploy ~328 MW of clean fuel power for data centers (reported in recent pre-market commentary), reinforcing Nebius as a scaled AI cloud / power user and attracting AI-infrastructure momentum flows.

Rapid post-IPO / carve‑out rerating as a pure-play AI cloud provider (ex-Yandex Nebius) with very high growth and very high cash burn, driving ‘story stock’ behavior and elevated volatility as AI-infrastructure names re-rate together.
summary: The recent 40–100%+ ramp in Nebius over the last 1–2 months is primarily a rerating on its AI-cloud narrative rather than a single new headline: investors are extrapolating the previously disclosed multiyear $17B Microsoft GPU-capacity deal and newer reports of a large Bloom Energy-backed 328 MW clean-power buildout into a long runway of AI-compute demand. As a vertically integrated, ex‑Yandex carve‑out positioned as an AI/HPC cloud specialist, NBIS is trading like a high-beta proxy on hyperscaler AI capex, with strong momentum (RSI in the 96th percentile) and low recent volume suggesting momentum/trend followers and AI-infrastructure flows are the main marginal buyers. The 1-day pullback despite still-elevated levels looks more like digestion/mean reversion after a parabolic multi-week move than a reaction to negative fundamental news.
